think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 31-year-old woman developed chronic, indolent unilateral gluteal and lower abdominal pain mimicking lumbar disc herniation following ultrasound-guided transvaginal oocyte retrieval, disguising a large communicating iliopsoas and gluteal cold abscess.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Presentation with chronic left gluteal and abdominal pain, localized tenderness, restricted hip movement, elevated ESR (53 mm/h), and MRI demonstrating communicating infectious lesions of the left iliac fossa and gluteal musculature, prior to surgical incision, drainage of caseous debris, and histopathological analysis.
3. Differential Distinctions: Lumbar disc herniation was ruled out by lack of response to conservative therapy and pelvic MRI showing muscular cystic masses; acute pyogenic abscess or brucellosis was ruled out by indolent 21-month course, lack of leukocytosis, negative blood and Brucella cultures, and discharge of caseous rather than purulent material upon surgical debridement.
case_prompt: A 31-year-old previously healthy woman presented with a 21-month history of progressive left gluteal pain accompanied by mild radiation down the left lower limb and restricted mobility of the left hip. Her symptoms began shortly after undergoing an ultrasound-guided transvaginal oocyte retrieval procedure at an outside fertility center, following which she noted lower abdominal discomfort and experienced a pregnancy loss. She had previously been treated conservatively for presumed lumbar disc herniation with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents and analgesic therapy without relief. She had no history of chronic medical illness and denied prior fever, respiratory symptoms, or known contacts with chronic infectious diseases. On physical examination, she was afebrile with normal vital signs. Palpation revealed marked localized tenderness over the left gluteal region and left lower abdomen, with mildly restricted range of motion of the left hip joint. Laboratory investigations revealed a white blood cell count of 3.51 × 10⁹/L with an absolute neutrophil count of 2.29 × 10⁹/L, C-reactive protein of 3.18 mg/dL, erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 53 mm/h, interleukin-6 of 12.3 pg/mL, and D-dimer of 0.63 mg/L. Musculoskeletal ultrasound demonstrated a cystic-solid mass within the left gluteus maximus communicating with the hip joint space, and pelvic MRI confirmed extensive communicating infectious collections involving the left iliac fossa and left gluteal musculature.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Chronic gluteal pain with radiating lower limb symptoms led to a prolonged misdiagnosis of lumbar disc displacement; however, conservative anti-inflammatory and neurotrophic therapies failed, and subsequent musculoskeletal ultrasound and pelvic MRI revealed communicating intramuscular infectious fluid collections rather than nerve root compression.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Because these symptoms were relatively mild and non-specific in the early stage, the patient initially sought care at an outside hospital, where she was misdiagnosed with lumbar disc herniation and received conservative treatment (Including anti-inflammatory and analgesic drugs, neurotrophic treatment, etc.), which failed to relieve her symptoms.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial abscess (e.g., Staphylococcal or Gram-negative pelvic abscess) / Brucellosis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: An indolent 21-month clinical course without acute sepsis or leukocytosis (WBC 3.51 × 10⁹/L), sterile 72-hour routine blood cultures, negative Brucella cultures, and surgical drainage showing caseous necrotic debris rather than foul-smelling acute purulence excluded common pyogenic and brucellar etiologies.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Postoperative laboratory evaluation showed a gradual decline in inflammatory markers. Blood culture demonstrated no bacterial growth after 72 h, and Brucella culture was negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Surgical exploration of the communicating iliac fossa and gluteus maximus lesions released 150 mL of caseous necrotic material with histological confirmation of caseating granulomatous inflammation, leading to prompt clinical resolution under quadruple antituberculous therapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Upon opening the capsule, approximately 100 mL of yellow, turbid fluid mixed with caseous necrotic material was released (Figure 2c)... Based on the gross intraoperative appearance, tuberculosis was strongly suspected.

editor_comments: Extrapulmonary tuberculous cold abscess involving the iliopsoas and gluteal compartments masquerading as lumbar disc disease following transvaginal oocyte retrieval.
